name: Three Leagues
alt: Free State of the Three Leagues
League of God's House, Grey League and League of the Ten Jurisdictions

successors.name: Helvetic Republic
successors.text: the Three Leagues, absorbed as the canton of Raetia; annexed 21 April 1799 (infobox)

successors.name: Cisalpine Republic
successors.text: the Valtellina, Chiavenna and Bormio, annexed 10 October 1797 (Three Leagues page) or 22 October (Cisalpine Republic page)

ledger.x: 1497: the Three Leagues become associates of the Old Swiss Confederacy.
1512: the Leagues take the Valtellina, Chiavenna and Bormio.
1512: the Valtellina, Chiavenna and Bormio become subject territory of the Three Leagues, the Confederacy's associate.
July 1620: the Valtellina rises against the Leagues.
July 1620: the Valtellina War begins ('Date: July 1620 - 5 March 1626').
July 1620: the Valtellina leaves the Three Leagues and so the associate's tint.
January 1622: the Leagues cede three valleys.
5 March 1626: the Treaty of Monzón ends the war.
3 September 1639: the Valtellina returns to the Leagues.
3 September 1639: the Valtellina returns to the Three Leagues and the tint resumes.
1652: the Lower Engadine buys its freedom from Austria.
1652 (bridging): the Müstair valley comes back from Austria.
October 1797: the Valtellina joins the Cisalpine Republic.
10 October 1797: the Valtellina leaves the Three Leagues and the tint ends.
1798: the Three Leagues cease to be associates of the Confederacy because the Confederacy fell to the French invasion of March 1798.
21 April 1799: the Three Leagues join the Helvetic Republic.

wars.name: Swabian War
wars.outcome: 'The Habsburgs were defeated at Calven Gorge and Dornach'; the Leagues sided with the Confederacy.

wars.name: Bündner Wirren
wars.outcome: 'Between 1618 and 1639 it became a battleground between competing factions': the Valtellina left the Leagues in July 1620 and returned on 3 September 1639; the Müstair, Lower Engadine and Prättigau were ceded in January 1622, the Prättigau came back within…

wars.name: Valtellina War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Monzón, 5 March 1626: the Valtelline got self-rule guaranteed by the Papacy, Spain and France; Spain and France had equal passage rights; 'The Grisons and Valtelline Protestants received nothing.'

certainty.note: Alpine valley jurisdictions and league boundaries, none surveyed on the pages opened; the Valtellina frontier with Milan is the same.

Sharp from the 1649-1652 treaties with Austria that fixed the Prättigau, Müstair and Lower Engadine (the last of them in 1652); the page gives no survey line, so this rests on those treaties and on the long-settled valley jurisdictions.
